notes: Cross-verse split with 1CO.1.24. Both verses carry the same construction, a dative pronoun with an articular substantive in apposition to it, recast by the ASV as a finite relative clause. 1CO.1.24 leaves the article unrepresented because αὐτοῖς has written the antecedent; this verse gave the article the relativizer 'who' while ἡμῖν took 'unto us'. Rule 32 gives the article the pronoun and nothing else and the participle the relativizer, and rule 20 names the identical case (Ὑμῖν ... τοῖς ἔθνεσιν -> to you that are Gentiles) as the one where the article is empty. Rule 90's single-word arm does not reach it, the ASV writing three words for the pair. s012 becomes unrepresented and s014 takes 'who are saved'.
